summary: Steel fire tower with an octagonal cupola near Brudenell, Lyndoch and Raglan; the cupola was restored at a Pembroke MNR office in 2003.

facts.design: Steel tower with an octagonal cupola

events.note: Cupola removed to the Pembroke MNR office and restored there; the source gives no date for the removal

evidence.supports: location near Brudenell, Lyndoch and Raglan
evidence.quote: Jamiesons Mountain, Brudenell, Lyndoch and Raglan, ON, Canada

evidence.supports: steel tower with an octagonal cupola
cupola removed to Pembroke MNR office and restored in 2003
evidence.quote: the Jamieson's Mtn. Tower's cupola was removed to the Pembroke MNR office and restored in 2003

evidence.supports: Ontario towers under the Department of Lands and Forests, later MNR (1972)
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: towers used less from the 1960s as aerial fire spotting, then firefighting crews, took over (aircraft did not take over firefighting)
evidence.quote: As the 1960s progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and then firefighting crews took over.
The decision ended up in removing many towers.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one listing (Firelookout.ca, which gives no year built, height or elevation) and one index line (Clayton Self's Ontario fire tower site) on the cupola. No source read gives a build date, builder, staffing, fire history or the tower's current state; the story says so only for what stands today. Two searches found nothing more on this tower. A Flickr Commons photo titled 'Jamieson Mountain Firetower' by Garnet Wilkes (Cloyne and District Historical Society, uploaded Oct 2022) was seen on a Flickr tag page; its licence and page were not checked, so it is not listed under photos. Do not confuse this tower with Mount Jamieson near Timmins (ca-on-kamistokia-hill), which is a different site in another part of Ontario.
